Master — area of study

Master in International Management

Train executives able to deepen their expertise in strategy, cross-cultural management, international development and leading cross-border operations, within an evolving regional and international economic environment.

This track is an area of study to be confirmed by the Direction before being displayed as an open admission: the curriculum, prerequisites, admission procedures and opening are all subject to validation. Contact the administration to check the status of this track for the relevant academic year.

Key information

DegreeMaster — 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 credits (LMD framework)
LocationBamako — Hamdallaye ACI 2000
LanguagesFrench / English (English every semester)
Indicative annual tuition1 500 000 FCFA / year (M1, M2) — written confirmation required for 2026–2027
Application fee15 000 FCFA
Thesis defence fee150 000 FCFA for the Master — amount to be confirmed for 2026–2027

Objectives

Deepen expertise in strategy as applied to activities conducted beyond national borders.

Develop cross-cultural management skills and the ability to lead the international development of an organisation, in line with the deepening and specialisation ethos of the ABS Master's cycle.

Skills developed

  • International strategy and management
  • Cross-cultural management
  • International business development
  • Leading cross-border operations

Skills derived strictly from the track's presentation sheet; the detailed curriculum and skills frameworks remain to be validated.

Admission requirements

Entry into Master 1:a Licence (Bachelor's degree) or recognised equivalent qualification in a relevant field, subject to review of the academic record (transcripts of the three years of the Licence, cover letter, curriculum vitae).

Entry into Master 2: Master 1 or an equivalent qualification in the field, subject to validation of prerequisites and the academic record.

Submitting an application does not guarantee automatic admission; every application is subject to review of the file and to the decision of the Office of Academic Affairs.

Indicative career outcomes

Indicatively, this Master's degree can prepare graduates for responsibilities linked to international development and leading cross-border operations within companies, institutions and organisations operating at the regional or international level, depending on each graduate's track and experience.

Career outcomes are perspectives, not guarantees of employment.

Would you like to apply for this Master's programme?

Contact the ABS team to confirm the admission requirements, supporting documents, key dates and available places.
